title: Abdominal Pain - Emergency Medicine
hpi_narrative: Ms. Y is a 50-year-old female with no significant past medical history who presents with severe abdominal pain. Onset is acute, the character is constant, and severity is high, associated with fever. Pertinent findings include severe pain on abdominal examination and tachycardia.

stacks.label: General Appearance
stacks.finding: Patient having severe pain – appropriate to look at patient to help guide diagnosis.

stacks.label: Abdomen
stacks.finding: This is the chief complaint, so this should be examined.

stacks.label: Bacterial culture, blood
stacks.finding: Fever and tachycardia after an abdominal surgery is worrisome, and therefore, a blood culture is warranted.

stacks.label: Bacterial culture, urine
stacks.finding: As the patient is experiencing abdominal pain, a urine culture is warranted to rule out genitourinary pathology.

stacks.label: CBC with differential
stacks.finding: Important to order a CBC with differential in a patient with a fever.

stacks.label: Urinalysis
stacks.finding: It's important to get an urinalysis to rule out bacterial infection and other causes of fever.
